objective: Determine whether matched-panel task-set separation depends on final-token prompt pooling and whether its depth profile persists or changes over the first eight generated-token updates.
model_selection_reason: Two current 7--9B checkpoints with exact branch hooks and different token-mixing implementations; this is a prespecified sensitivity subset, not a cross-model population sample.

sample_identity.source: Use the exact 100 frozen document IDs per task from the parent experiment.
sample_identity.decoding: Deterministic and unchanged from the parent experiment.

conditions.name: mean_prompt_prefill
conditions.source: New extraction with observer parity checked.

conditions.name: first_cached_decode_update
conditions.source: New extraction with observer parity and per-task decode coverage checked.
conditions.estimand: The cached one-token forward conditioned on the first generated answer token; this state predicts the second token. It is not the state that produced the first answer token.

conditions.name: generated_response_trajectory
conditions.source: New position-resolved extraction with observer parity and per-step coverage checked.
conditions.trajectory_estimand: One vector per example, layer, stream, and generated-token update for absolute decode steps 0 through 7. Each step is analyzed separately; no class-dependent token or step pooling is allowed.

real_model_smoke.interpretation: The engineering gate passes for the last prompt state and the first cached decode update. The frozen direct-answer stop rules produce no later common response step, so the planned eight-step contrast is not estimable in this protocol.

analysis.comparison: Compare complete layer--stream profiles and selection-aware Fisher/probe randomization within model across prefill, first decode, and each absolute decode step; do not pool models or response positions.
analysis.trajectory_summary: Report the layer-stream-step maximum only with a randomization null that repeats selection over every included layer, stream, and step. Also report a prespecified area under the per-step depth-mean curve over steps with complete coverage.
analysis.missingness: Report response-length coverage by task and class at every step. The primary trajectory comparison uses only a prespecified common step prefix with at least 95% coverage in every task; later steps are descriptive and may not use a class-dependent subset.

promotion_gates: A two-task real-model smoke must show exact layer/stream semantics and tracker-off/on response parity.

Every included example must have one first_update decode record at every selected layer and stream; this is the first cached update after one answer token, not the state that generated that first token. Otherwise report coverage and do not compare a selected subset as if it were complete.

Every emitted all_updates record must have an explicit zero-based decode_step, one update, and exact task/sample identity. The per-step record count must equal the number of responses reaching that step times the selected layer and stream count.
Response length is an outcome of the model and can differ by task set. Report its distribution and do not interpret later-step separation unless coverage is balanced under the frozen rule.
Prefill records captured in the both-phase run must reproduce the reference condition under identical pooling and batch settings.
All conditions must preserve prompts, sample IDs, batch size, generation settings, storage dtype, and model revision.
claim_limit: A pooling- or response-position-dependent result concerns the estimator and generated trajectory under this direct-answer protocol. It does not identify a distinct reasoning mechanism; absolute token steps are not aligned semantic reasoning steps. Any multi-step explanation study must use a separate frozen prompt and may not be presented as an extension of the direct-answer result.
